title: Netflix's India revenue grows 18% as viewing hours jump 24%: what drove it
subtitle: A jail-themed reality show and a Flipkart shopping deal gave Netflix its best quarter ever for new paying members in India.
content_html:
Picture every Netflix screen in India, from phones on a college bus to TVs in a family living room. Now imagine all of them together watching for almost a quarter more time than a year ago. That is what happened between July and September 2026. In its letter to shareholders dated 20 October 2026, Netflix said total viewing hours in India grew 24% and its India revenue grew about 18% compared with the same three months of 2025. The Economic Times reported the India numbers on 21 October.

So what pushed it? A jail-themed reality show, a shopping app and a few hit series. Here is the story, in plain words.

First, what are viewing hours?

Viewing hours are simple. Add up every hour that every person spent watching Netflix in India. If you watch two episodes of one hour each, you add two hours to the pile. If a million people do that, the pile grows by two million hours.

India's pile grew 24% in one year. Think of a chai stall that sold 100 cups a day last year and now sells 124 cups a day.

But there is a twist. Netflix said that view hours per member grew only in the low to mid single digits. That means each person is watching only a little more than before. So most of the jump came from more people joining, not from each person watching much longer. More customers at the chai stall, not bigger cups.

Revenue is not profit

Revenue is all the money that comes in. For Netflix, that is mostly what members pay each month for their plans, plus money from ads. Profit is what is left after paying all the costs, like making shows and paying staff.

Picture a samosa stall. If it sells samosas worth ₹1,000 in a day, that is revenue. If potatoes, oil, rent and the helper's pay cost ₹700, the profit is ₹300. A stall can have big revenue and still make little profit.

For India, Netflix only shared the growth rate. It did not share India revenue in rupees or dollars, and it did not say how many paying members it added. It also said the 18% is on an "F/X neutral" basis. F/X means foreign exchange, the rate at which rupees turn into dollars. "Neutral" means Netflix removed the effect of that rate moving up or down, so the number shows real growth, not a currency swing.

The show that drove it: Lock Upp

Netflix gave most of the credit to its shows. The biggest was Lock Upp, which Netflix called its first daily reality series. Netflix said it drove the most viewing of any title on Netflix in India ever, based on view hours in the first 91 days.

In Lock Upp, celebrity contestants are kept together in a pretend jail and have to get through challenges and audience votes. According to What's on Netflix, the show spent two weeks in Netflix's global Top 10 for non English TV with over 34 million hours viewed in that time. It reached number 1 in India and stayed in India's daily Top 10 for 41 days. A second season has been confirmed, with Farah Khan and Riteish Deshmukh returning as hosts.

Two scripted series also helped: Musafir Cafe and Operation Safed Sagar. Netflix listed both alongside Lock Upp in the same letter.

The Flipkart trick: watch Netflix by shopping

The second push came from shopping. On 31 July 2026, Flipkart and Netflix announced a deal that went live on 1 August. Flipkart Plus members who place four orders of ₹299 or more in a calendar month unlock a Netflix Mobile plan for the next 30 days. No extra payment. After 30 days, they have to earn it again.

Orders on Flipkart, Flipkart Grocery and Flipkart Minutes all count. Shoppers who are not Plus members yet qualify after 15 orders in 12 months. Flipkart said it is the first time in Indian e-commerce that Netflix can be earned through everyday shopping. Netflix called it its first e-commerce partnership in India.

This is called a loyalty bundle. A loyalty programme rewards you for coming back again and again, like a stamp card at a juice shop where the tenth juice is free. Here, the free thing is a month of Netflix.

Netflix said that this transaction-based loyalty bundle with Flipkart, together with its shows, gave it its largest quarter ever of paid net additions in India. Paid net additions means new paying members minus members who left. It is like counting how many more students are in a class at the end of the term than at the start.

Why India matters to Netflix

When the Flipkart deal was announced, Laurent Uguen, a Netflix vice president for partnerships in Asia Pacific, said "India is one of the most exciting entertainment markets in the world."

In its letter, Netflix also pointed to India as proof that its plan works. It said its business in India in the quarter was an example of strong results when it executes well on its core strategy. Netflix also said it wants viewing hours to grow faster around the world, and is confident it can do that.

The bigger Netflix picture

Around the world, Netflix's revenue for July to September 2026 was $12.87 billion, up 11.8% from $11.51 billion a year earlier. Its operating income, the profit from running the business before things like tax, rose to $4.46 billion from $3.25 billion.

Its operating margin was 34.6%, up from 28.2%. Margin is the share of each rupee of revenue that stays as profit. A 34.6% margin means that out of every ₹100 coming in, about ₹34.60 was left after running costs.

Not everything went up. Netflix cut its 2026 ad revenue estimate to about $2.7 billion from about $3 billion, saying some ad tools were rolling out a little slower than planned. For the full year 2026, it expects revenue of $51.1 billion, up 13%. It also plans to bring its plan with ads to 15 more countries in 2027, with the first launches in March.

Netflix said its audience worldwide is approaching one billion people.

What to take away

  • Total viewing in India grew 24%, mostly because more people joined.
  • India revenue grew about 18%, faster than Netflix's roughly 12% growth worldwide.
  • Lock Upp became the most watched title on Netflix in India ever, by first 91 days of viewing.
  • A shopping deal with Flipkart helped Netflix have its best quarter ever for new paying members in India.
